themes.summary: Alex proved that identical audio input produces meaningfully different memory cards across re-imports — different tags, different dates, fabricated attributions. For an app whose core promise is reliable memory, this is not a polish issue; it is a trust-killer that Alex explicitly ties to not paying and not recommending.

themes.theme: App does not learn the user over time
themes.summary: Both Margaret and Priya independently hit the same wall: the app on day 22 feels identical to the app on day 1. No follow-up questions, no reference to past entries, no personalisation. Priya frames this as a moat question; Margaret describes it as the product feeling like a recording device that has never met her. This is the same signal from two very different users.

themes.theme: Capture and search are genuinely strong — and paying intent is real
themes.summary: Daniel is already paying the $9 tier and explicitly offered to upgrade to $20+ for a memory-export feature. Priya and Margaret both praised transcription accuracy. The core capture loop works. The positive signal is real and concentrated around parents and people with rich relationship memories.

critical_objections.objection: Same audio file produces different memory cards on re-import — different tags, dates, and fabricated attributions — making the product untrustworthy for its core use case.
The product feels like a better wrapper over ChatGPT + Notion, with no differentiation that justifies a paid subscription over a DIY alternative.

After three weeks of use, the app still feels like a recording device that has never met the user — no prompts, no follow-ups, no memory of prior entries — causing Margaret to stop using it in week 2.

must_fix_for_g4: Fix non-deterministic output: pin temperature/seed and cache structured output keyed on audio hash so identical input always produces identical memory cards.

Ship at least a v1 personalisation signal: the app must reference prior entries in some visible way (e.g. 'you mentioned Leo last week — want to add to this?') so users feel the product is learning them, not just storing files.
Fix people-tagging attribution errors: the fabricated speaker attribution Alex logged and the misattributed quote are accuracy bugs in a domain where accuracy is the product's entire value claim.
Build the memory-export / capsule feature Daniel is explicitly willing to pay more for — this is the clearest upgrade-revenue signal in the dataset.
nice_to_have_post_launch: Daily or contextual prompts for users who don't know what to record (Margaret's explicit ask — likely valuable for any user over 40).
iOS Share Extension support on iPad (Priya flagged, minor).
Fix first-recording audio drop after phone restart (Alex flagged, minor).
Shared/family thread view so partners like Daniel's wife can co-contribute to the same memory graph.
Fix date-search fuzzy-match returning adjacent dates that don't match the query.
next_sprint_brief: The single most urgent thing this week is the non-deterministic output bug Alex documented — same .m4a in, three different memory cards out, including a fabricated attribution. That is not a minor bug; it is the product lying to users, and Alex has already said it blocks both payment and recommendation. Start there: pin temperature, cache structured output on audio hash, and verify with Alex's test files before touching anything else. Once that is solid, the second priority is shipping the earliest possible version of personalisation — Margaret stopped using the app at week 2 specifically because it felt like a recording device that had never met her, and Priya named the same gap as her reason for not paying. Even a simple "you mentioned [person] last week — want to add to that?" surfaces in the UI and would directly address both partners. Daniel is your clearest path to G4 revenue signal: he is already on the $9 tier and has offered to go to $20+ for a memory-export capsule feature — scope and ship a minimal version of that before Mother's Day if at all possible.

kill_signal_flags.triggered_by: I got back three meaningfully different memory summaries — different tags, different inferred dates… and one summary attributed a quote to a person whose name was never spoken in the audio.
kill_signal_flags.rationale: Identical input producing fabricated attributions and inconsistent structured outputs is a direct accuracy failure in a domain — personal memory — where users must be able to trust every field on every card.

kill_signal_flags.triggered_by: The app on day 22 felt exactly like the app on day one — just with more files inside it. / There's no 'Priya's Eterna is different from Daniel's Eterna' yet.
kill_signal_flags.rationale: Both Margaret and Priya independently described a product that accumulates data but does not adapt or personalise from it — the core definition of a missing data loop.

kill_signal_flags.triggered_by: I could probably build 80% of this with ChatGPT and a Notion template in a weekend… what's the moat?
kill_signal_flags.rationale: Priya directly asked the moat question and answered it herself — the product is currently a well-executed wrapper with no durable differentiation she could identify.

g4_readiness_rationale: Three Kill Signals are firing simultaneously — accuracy floor, data loop, and moat — and two of the three paying-intent blockers are unresolved. Daniel is the one bright spot: he is already paying and has a specific upgrade trigger. Reema gave two sentences and was excluded from theme weighting. Fix the determinism bug and ship a visible personalisation signal before G4 is realistic.
